newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU mum on Coca-Cola Enterprises.
newsitem.headline: EU mum on Coca-Cola Enterprises.

text.p: The European Commission declined to comment Friday on Virgin Cola's allegations that a British bottler of soft drinks that is the takeovber target of Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc. is abusing its dominant position.

The European Union's competition watchdog also refused to unveil details about objections that it is expected to file shortly against Coca-Cola Enterprises's proposed takeover of Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages Ltd, sticking to its policy of discretion in cases undergoing an in-depth probe.

The European Commission, the EU's executive body, said in September that it was starting the so-called second stage of proceedings into the proposed deal to assess the impact of the acquisition on competition for soft drinks in Britain.
Lawyers well versed in EU competition law stressed that it is normal procedure to follow that with a statement of objections detailing its grievances.

Coca-Cola Enterprises, the world's biggest bottler of Coca-Cola soft drinks, said in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it expected an EU statement before the end of November.

The opening of a detailed inquiry, which lasts up to four months, into a merger usually means that the deal is unlikely to get EU clearance without being changed. This often means selling off some businesses to avoid creation or strengthening of dominant positions.

Virgin Cola, part of the Virgin Group run by millionaire entrepreneur Richard Branson, said Thursday it would complain to the Commission about what it sees as Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages Ltd's abuse of its dominant position in Britain's cola market.
